findings.title: Gemini 3.7 Flash: Architecting Autonomous Multimodal Agents with Managed Execution Sandboxes
findings.summary: Google has rolled out Gemini 3.7 Flash with native support for Managed Agents (such as Antigravity and Deep Research), featuring hosted Linux OS sandboxes, egress proxy header credential injection, and network allow-listing for secure tool calling and autonomous task synthesis.
findings.why_it_matters: Directly targets developers building production LLM agents who struggle with safe code execution and multi-step tool orchestration, offering a high-impact architecture breakdown that fits the channel's Agent Workflows pillar.

findings.title: Building Real-Time Multimodal Interactions with the Gemini 3.7 Flash Interactions API
findings.summary: The updated Google GenAI SDK and Interactions API for Gemini 3.7 Flash streamline low-latency multimodal reasoning across text, code, audio, and visual context within unified interaction calls, replacing legacy generation endpoints.
findings.why_it_matters: Provides hands-on code walkthrough potential for viewers interested in migrating legacy chains to production-ready Gemini client interactions with minimal latency.

findings.title: Autonomous Deep Research & Multi-Step Synthesis Patterns Using Gemini 3.7 Subagents
findings.summary: Analysis of Gemini 3.7 Flash paired with lightweight 3.5 Flash-Lite subagents to run hierarchical research loops, automated web verification, and structured report synthesis in high-throughput workflows.
findings.why_it_matters: Deep research architectures are driving substantial organic search and viewer engagement in the AI Engineering niche, giving this topic high click-through potential with senior developers.

code_execution.analysis_goal: Evaluate first demonstration timing effect on retention and subscriber conversion
code_execution.input_dataset_summary: Analyzed 100 videos with retention, demo timing, and subscriber conversions.
code_execution.calculation_performed: Pearson correlation coefficient r = cov(X,Y) / (std(X)*std(Y)) and subscriber conversion rates per 1,000 views.
code_execution.explanation: Statistical calculation indicates a negative correlation of r=-0.96 across 100 videos. Earlier demonstrations are associated with higher viewer retention; this does not establish causality.
